modules.title: Phishing Email Identification
modules.description: Learn to identify and respond to phishing emails effectively.

lessons.title: Introduction to Phishing
lessons.content: Phishing is a cyber attack that uses disguised email as a weapon. The goal is to trick the email recipient into believing that the message is something they want or need.

lessons.title: Red Flags in Phishing Emails
lessons.content: Common signs include: urgent language, spelling/grammar errors, suspicious sender addresses, unexpected attachments, and requests for personal information.

lessons.title: Practice Exercise
lessons.content: Examine the following emails and identify which ones are phishing attempts.

questions.question: Which of the following is a common sign of a phishing email?
questions.explanation: Phishing emails often use urgent language to pressure recipients into acting quickly without thinking.

questions.question: What should you do if you receive a suspicious email?
questions.explanation: Always report suspicious emails to your IT security team. Never click links or forward to others.

questions.question: What does 'spoofing' mean in the context of phishing?

options.text: Disguising email to appear from a trusted source

questions.explanation: Spoofing involves falsifying email headers to make messages appear to come from someone the recipient trusts.

modules.title: Password Security Best Practices
modules.description: Master the art of creating and managing secure passwords.

lessons.title: Why Passwords Matter
lessons.content: Passwords are your first line of defense against unauthorized access. Weak passwords account for over 80% of security breaches.

lessons.title: Understanding Password Strength
lessons.content: Strong passwords use a mix of uppercase, lowercase, numbers, and symbols. They should be at least 12 characters long.

lessons.title: Password Management Tools
lessons.content: Password managers help you create and store unique, complex passwords for every account.

questions.question: What is the recommended minimum length for a secure password?
questions.explanation: Modern security standards recommend passwords of at least 12 characters for adequate protection.

questions.question: Which of the following is the strongest password?
questions.explanation: Passphrases using random words are longer and harder to crack than shorter complex passwords.

questions.question: Why should you avoid reusing passwords across multiple accounts?
questions.explanation: If one account is breached, attackers will try the same password on your other accounts.

modules.title: Social Engineering Awareness
modules.description: Recognize and defend against social engineering tactics.

lessons.title: What is Social Engineering?
lessons.content: Social engineering is the psychological manipulation of people into performing actions or divulging confidential information.

lessons.title: Common Social Engineering Techniques
lessons.content: Techniques include pretexting, baiting, tailgating, quid pro quo, and vishing (voice phishing).

lessons.title: Defending Against Social Engineering
lessons.content: Always verify identities, be cautious with requests for information, and follow proper authentication procedures.

questions.question: What is 'pretexting' in social engineering?

options.text: Creating a fake scenario to gain trust
Calling pretending to be IT support

questions.explanation: Pretexting involves creating a fabricated scenario to engage victims and gain their trust.

questions.question: Someone calls claiming to be from IT and asks for your password. What should you do?

options.text: Provide the password if they sound legitimate
Hang up and call IT directly using official number
Give them a hint instead of full password

questions.explanation: Always verify identity through independent channels. IT will never ask for your password.

questions.question: What is 'tailgating' in physical security?

options.text: Following someone through a secure door

questions.explanation: Tailgating is following an authorized person through a secure entry point without proper credentials.

modules.title: Data Handling & Protection
modules.description: Learn proper procedures for handling sensitive data.

lessons.title: Data Classification
lessons.content: Data is classified into categories: Public, Internal, Confidential, and Restricted based on sensitivity.

lessons.title: Proper Data Handling
lessons.content: Different data types require different handling procedures for storage, transmission, and disposal.

lessons.title: Data Breach Response
lessons.content: Know the steps to take if you suspect a data breach has occurred.

questions.question: Which data classification is the most sensitive?
questions.explanation: Restricted is the highest classification for the most sensitive data.

questions.question: How should you dispose of documents containing confidential information?
questions.explanation: Confidential documents should be cross-cut shredded to prevent reconstruction.

questions.question: What is the first step if you suspect a data breach?

options.text: Wait and see if it resolves

questions.explanation: Always report suspected breaches immediately to allow proper containment and investigation.

modules.title: Physical Security Awareness
modules.description: Protect your workspace and equipment from physical threats.

lessons.title: Why Physical Security Matters
lessons.content: Physical security is the foundation of all other security measures. Without it, digital protections can be bypassed.

lessons.title: Best Practices
lessons.content: Lock screens, secure devices, clean desk policy, and visitor management are essential physical security practices.

lessons.title: Reporting Security Concerns
lessons.content: Know how to report suspicious activity, lost devices, or security incidents.

questions.question: What should you do when leaving your desk?
questions.explanation: Always lock your screen (Windows+L) when leaving your desk to prevent unauthorized access.

questions.question: What is a 'clean desk policy'?

options.text: Removing all sensitive documents and materials at end of day

questions.explanation: A clean desk policy requires securing all sensitive materials when not in use or at end of day.

questions.question: You notice a stranger in a restricted area. What should you do?
questions.explanation: Always report unauthorized individuals in restricted areas to security personnel.
